slides.title: Turn and move
slides.notes: Seven terms for turning a camera or moving it.

slides.title: Pan, tilt, roll
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: Each camera turns and its position never changes. Pan is left and right, tilt is up and down, roll tips the horizon. In-view posts turn red, so you see what the turn brings into frame.
slides.picture: Three small diagrams. In each the camera turns while its position stays fixed.

new_texts: Turn left or right on the spot; position unchanged.
turns on the spot; the camera stays where it is
slides sideways; the camera changes place
all_texts: Turn left or right on the spot; position unchanged.

slides sideways; the camera changes place

new_texts: Spin around the viewing direction; the horizon tips.

slides.title: Dolly, truck, pedestal
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: The camera moves and keeps facing the same way. Dolly is forward and back along the view, truck is sideways, pedestal is straight up and down. Distances are in metres at 100 px per metre.
slides.picture: A top view where the camera moves forward then back, then sideways, and a side view where it moves up and down. The view direction never changes.

slides.title: Orbit
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: Step one: the camera moves on a circle and stays aimed at the subject, so the distance stays 1.90 m. Step two: the same angle done as a pan on the spot loses the subject.
slides.picture: A top view. Step one: the camera moves along a circle around the subject, always aimed at it. Step two: the camera turns on the spot and the subject leaves the view.

new_texts: camera at (1.22, 1.46) m from the subject
Move around a subject on a curved path while keeping it framed.
moves around the subject, keeps it framed
turns on the spot, may lose the subject
Orbit: the camera sweeps 140° on a circle 1.90 m from the subject and stays aimed at it. The subject stays in the frame.

slides.title: The lens
slides.notes: Seven terms about what the lens does, and how it differs from moving.

slides.title: Zoom, focal length, field of view
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: The camera never moves. Angle = 2 atan(18 / mm) for a 36 mm wide sensor, an assumption stated on the slide.
slides.picture: A camera fixed at the left. Its view cone narrows as focal length grows. A table lists focal lengths with the angle each gives. Then a wider angle takes in more of the nine posts.

new_texts: Change the lens (field of view or focal length); the camera does not move.
changes the lens; the camera stays put
moves the camera; the lens stays the same
Zoom: the cone narrows. The camera does not move.

slides.title: Dolly versus zoom
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: Scene numbers: house 3 m away, tower 9 m away, 240 px focal scale. A 1.2 m dolly gives the house x1.67 and the tower x1.15. A x1.67 zoom gives both x1.67. The size ratio house to tower changes only in the dolly.
slides.picture: Two views of the same scene, a near house and a far tower. In the dolly the camera moves 1.2 metres forward. In the zoom the lens magnifies by the same factor on the house.

new_texts: A dolly changes parallax (near and far shift against each other); a zoom only magnifies.
Dolly: the camera moves 1.2 m forward. The near house grows ×1.67. The far tower grows only ×1.15.
all_texts: A dolly changes parallax (near and far shift against each other); a zoom only magnifies.
Dolly: the camera moves 1.2 m forward. The near house grows ×1.67. The far tower grows only ×1.15.

new_texts: Zoom: the lens magnifies ×1.67, the camera stays put. The house grows the same as in the dolly, and the tower grows ×1.67.
all_texts: A dolly changes parallax (near and far shift against each other); a zoom only magnifies.
Zoom: the lens magnifies ×1.67, the camera stays put. The house grows the same as in the dolly, and the tower grows ×1.67.

new_texts: Same house, different tower. In the dolly the house-to-tower size ratio changes. In the zoom it does not.
all_texts: A dolly changes parallax (near and far shift against each other); a zoom only magnifies.
Same house, different tower. In the dolly the house-to-tower size ratio changes. In the zoom it does not.

slides.title: Parallax
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: Shift in the picture = 220 px x 1 m / distance. Near 2 m: 110 px. Mid 4 m: 55 px. Far 8 m: 27.5 px.
slides.picture: A top view of a camera moving one metre to the right past three posts in a line. Beside it, the picture: the near post moves furthest.

new_texts: Nearer things shift more than farther things when the viewpoint moves.
scales everything by the same factor
The camera slides 1 m right. The three posts were lined up. Now they fan out in the picture.
all_texts: Nearer things shift more than farther things when the viewpoint moves.
scales everything by the same factor
The camera slides 1 m right. The three posts were lined up. Now they fan out in the picture.

new_texts: Half the distance, twice the shift. The 2 m post moves 110 px, the 8 m post 28 px.
all_texts: Nearer things shift more than farther things when the viewpoint moves.
scales everything by the same factor
Half the distance, twice the shift. The 2 m post moves 110 px, the 8 m post 28 px.

slides.title: Perspective and orthographic
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: Perspective box width = 260 px / distance: 87, 58, 40, 29, 20 px. Orthographic: 44 px every time.
slides.picture: Two rows of identical boxes at five distances. In perspective they shrink and the rows converge. In orthographic every box is the same size and the rows stay parallel.

new_texts: same boxes, same size in the world
Distant things shrink / size does not depend on distance.
size does not depend on distance
Perspective: the same 1 m box looks 87 px wide at 3 m and 20 px wide at 13 m. The rows meet at the horizon.
all_texts: same boxes, same size in the world
Distant things shrink / size does not depend on distance.
size does not depend on distance
Perspective: the same 1 m box looks 87 px wide at 3 m and 20 px wide at 13 m. The rows meet at the horizon.

new_texts: Orthographic: every box is 44 px wide whatever its distance. The rows never meet.
all_texts: Distant things shrink / size does not depend on distance.
size does not depend on distance
Orthographic: every box is 44 px wide whatever its distance. The rows never meet.

slides.title: Following the action
slides.notes: Six terms about how the camera tracks a moving target.

slides.title: Follow camera and smoothing
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: Exponential smoothing with a 0.25 s time constant, stepped at 60 frames per second. Peak lag is computed from the simulation.
slides.picture: Two lanes. In the first the view window is locked to a moving target. In the second the window trails the target and catches up after it stops.

slides.title: Deadzone and look-ahead
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: Deadzone half-width 70 px. Look-ahead: lead 0.5 s at 200 px/s gives 100 px, eased in with a 0.25 s time constant.
slides.picture: A screen frame with a dashed deadzone box. The target moves right. The camera stays still until the target reaches the edge of the box. Then the frame shifts ahead of a moving target.

slides.title: Screen shake
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.notes: Amplitude 18 px, decay constant 0.18 s, random direction each frame from a fixed seed so replays match. 5% is reached at ln(20) x 0.18 = 0.54 s.
slides.picture: A view that shakes for 0.6 seconds. A graph of the sideways offset stays inside a falling envelope.

new_texts: Brief, fading random offset of the camera for impact.
a brief offset that fades out
removes jerk instead of adding it
A hit lands. The view jumps by up to 18 px in a random direction, and the jump shrinks every frame.

slides.title: Before you give a camera instruction
slides.source: Source: CSYE 7270 midterm glossary, “Camera” section. Not explained in the chapters.
slides.picture: A checklist of six items drawn one at a time.

new_texts: Is the camera moving (dolly, truck, pedestal, orbit) or turning (pan, tilt, roll)?
Is it the legs or the lens: a dolly moves the camera, a zoom changes the lens?
Did I name the axis, the direction, how far or how many degrees, how long, and the easing?
For a follower: smoothing amount, deadzone size, look-ahead, and camera limits?
For a hit: shake size, how long, and that it fades to zero?
Lens and projection: focal length or field of view, perspective or orthographic?
Then say it exactly: “dolly in 2 m, 1.5 seconds, ease-out”, not “swoop in”.
